# Code of Conduct

## Our standards

Seismic Atlas welcomes respectful participation from people of all backgrounds
and experience levels. Examples of positive behavior include:

- giving specific, constructive, and evidence-based feedback;
- respecting different levels of technical and scientific knowledge;
- acknowledging data sources and prior work;
- focusing criticism on ideas and implementations, not people;
- protecting private and security-sensitive information.

Harassment, discrimination, personal attacks, threats, deliberate disruption,
and publishing another person's private information are not acceptable.

## Scientific and public-safety discussions

Earthquake information can affect public trust. Participants must not present
speculation as official guidance, use the project to spread alarm, or imply
that Seismic Atlas is an AFAD warning, hazard-assessment, or forecasting
service.

## Enforcement

Project maintainers may edit or remove contributions that violate these
standards and may temporarily or permanently restrict participation. Report a
conduct concern privately using a contact method listed on the maintainer's
[GitHub profile](https://github.com/frknuynk). Do not publish sensitive conduct
reports in a public issue.

Maintainers will handle reports as confidentially as practical and will seek a
proportionate, fair response based on the available evidence.
